item.content:encoded:
The Youth Envoys Greece 2027 programme is inviting changemakers, innovators, students, professionals, youth advocates, policymakers and emerging leaders from around the world to participate in an international leadership and diplomacy experience in Athens, Greece, from 21 to 24 January 2027.

Under its Direct Access Participation category: participants can apply for a confirmed seat at the programme, with the organisers stating that an invitation letter, sponsorship letter, embassy recommendation and visa-support documents will be provided under this participation category.

The four-day event is positioned as more than a conventional conference. It is presented as an international platform where participants from different backgrounds and countries can come together to build connections, exchange ideas, develop leadership capabilities and engage with a global community of changemakers.

The programme explicitly states that it is open to all nationalities and all ages, making it a potentially broad international opportunity for individuals interested in leadership, diplomacy, global engagement and personal development.

Youth Envoys Greece 2027 at a Glance

For individuals searching for international conferences, leadership programmes and diplomacy opportunities in Europe, the key information about Youth Envoys Greece 2027 includes:

  • Programme: Youth Envoys Greece 2027
  • Participation category: Direct Access Participation
  • Location: Athens, Greece
  • Dates: 21–24 January 2027
  • Duration: Four days
  • Focus: Leadership and diplomacy
  • Nationality: Open to all nationalities
  • Age: All ages eligible
  • Participation feature: Confirmed seat
  • Documents stated by the organiser: Invitation letter, sponsorship letter, embassy recommendation and visa-support documents
  • Application deadline: Not stated on the supplied page.

What Is Youth Envoys Greece 2027?

Youth Envoys Greece 2027 is presented as an international leadership and diplomacy programme taking place in Athens.

The organisers describe the event as an opportunity for people who want to step onto an international platform and become part of a global community of individuals working toward positive change.

The programme’s messaging centres on the idea that today’s changemakers and emerging leaders have an important role to play in shaping the next chapter of global change.

Rather than presenting the experience solely as a traditional conference, the programme emphasises participation, leadership, diplomacy, networking and exposure to an international community.

The event is scheduled to take place over four days, from 21 to 24 January 2027, giving participants an opportunity to spend several days engaged in the programme in Athens.

Direct Access Participation Explained

The opportunity is specifically promoted under the Direct Access Participation category.

According to the supplied page, this category is intended to provide participants with a confirmed seat at the event rather than leaving participation uncertain.

The organisers state that participants under this category will receive:

  • A confirmed seat.
  • An invitation letter.
  • A sponsorship letter.
  • An embassy recommendation.
  • Visa-support documents.

These documents are presented as part of the Direct Access Participation arrangement and are intended to support participants in preparing for international participation in Athens.

The page specifically states that the invitation letter, sponsorship letter, embassy recommendation and visa-support documents will be provided under this category.

Applicants should nevertheless carefully review the official terms and application information before making travel or financial commitments, particularly because the supplied page does not provide detailed information about the precise scope or monetary value of the stated sponsorship.

Who Can Participate in Youth Envoys Greece 2027?

One of the most notable aspects of the opportunity is its broad eligibility.

The programme states that it is

Open to all nationalities.

It also states:

All ages are eligible.

This means that the opportunity is not restricted to applicants from a particular country, region or continent, nor does the supplied page impose a specific age bracket.

The programme specifically mentions several categories of people who may find the experience relevant.

These include:

  • Students.
  • Professionals.
  • Youth advocates.
  • Policymakers.
  • Emerging leaders.
  • Changemakers.
  • Innovators.
  • Other individuals interested in leadership and global engagement.

The broad participant profile means that the programme is not presented as being exclusively for university students or young people. Instead, people from different professional and educational backgrounds and of different ages are invited to consider participation.

Is Youth Envoys Greece 2027 Open to International Applicants?

Yes. The supplied information explicitly states that the programme is open to all nationalities.

This gives the opportunity a genuinely international scope, with prospective participants able to apply from countries across Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America and other parts of the world.

The application form itself contains an extensive list of countries and territories under both nationality and country of residence, including countries such as Kenya, South Africa, Nigeria, Ghana, Rwanda, Tanzania, Uganda, India, Canada, the United Kingdom, the United States, Australia, France, Germany and Greece, among many others.

The page does not identify any race, ethnicity or continental restriction.

Is There an Age Limit for Youth Envoys Greece 2027?

The programme states that all ages are eligible.

This is important because the name “Youth Envoys” might otherwise suggest that the programme is limited to a particular youth age bracket.

However, based on the supplied page, no specific maximum or minimum age is stated. Instead, the event explicitly promotes participation as being open to people of all ages.

The programme also gives examples of participants ranging from students and youth advocates to professionals, policymakers and emerging leaders.

What Is the Main Focus of the Programme?

Youth Envoys Greece 2027 focuses broadly on leadership and diplomacy.

The event is intended to provide an international environment where participants can interact with other changemakers, innovators and future leaders.

The organisers frame the programme around several interconnected ideas:

  • Leadership development.
  • International engagement.
  • Diplomacy.
  • Building alliances.
  • Cross-border networking.
  • Personal growth.
  • Sharing ideas.
  • Creating meaningful change.
  • Becoming part of a global community.

The programme’s description encourages participants to challenge existing boundaries, establish new connections and develop their ability to contribute to change.

This makes the event potentially relevant to people whose professional or personal interests involve international relations, diplomacy, leadership, youth development, public policy, social impact, innovation or global cooperation.

Why Attend an International Leadership and Diplomacy Programme?

International leadership programmes can expose participants to perspectives and experiences that may not be available within their immediate professional or academic environments.

Youth Envoys Greece 2027 is designed around an international gathering, meaning participants have the opportunity to interact with people from different countries and backgrounds.

For participants, this type of environment can support:

International Networking

Participants can connect with other individuals who share an interest in leadership, diplomacy and positive social change.

Building relationships with people from different countries can help broaden an individual’s understanding of international issues and create opportunities for future collaboration.

Leadership Exposure

The programme is specifically presented as a leadership experience.

For emerging leaders, participation can provide an opportunity to develop confidence, exchange ideas and position themselves within an international community.

Cross-Cultural Engagement

Because the programme welcomes participants from all nationalities, the event has an inherently international character.

Participants can engage with individuals who may have different perspectives, experiences, cultures and approaches to solving social and global challenges.

Diplomacy and Global Engagement

The programme’s focus on diplomacy can be particularly relevant to people interested in international relations, policy, public service, advocacy and global affairs.

Personal and Professional Growth

The organisers describe the programme as an opportunity for participants to grow beyond what they previously thought possible.

The event is therefore positioned not simply as a place to attend sessions but as an experience intended to encourage participants to expand their networks, perspectives and leadership ambitions.

What Does the Athens Experience Involve?

The programme will take place in Athens, Greece, from 21–24 January 2027.

Athens provides the physical setting for the four-day leadership and diplomacy programme.

The event is described as a four-day experience, meaning participants are expected to attend during the scheduled programme period.

The supplied page does not provide a detailed day-by-day agenda or session schedule. Therefore, applicants should consult the official programme materials for additional information about the specific activities, speakers, sessions and daily timetable.

Who Could Benefit from Youth Envoys Greece 2027?

Although the programme is open to all ages and nationalities, certain profiles may find it particularly relevant.

Students

Students interested in leadership, diplomacy, international affairs, public policy, social impact or global development may find the programme relevant to their interests.

Participation could provide exposure to an international environment beyond their academic institution.

Young Professionals

Professionals seeking to expand their international network may use the event as an opportunity to connect with people working across different sectors and countries.

Youth Advocates

Individuals involved in youth advocacy can potentially benefit from connecting with other changemakers and exchanging experiences concerning youth participation and leadership.

Policymakers

The programme may also be relevant to policymakers interested in international dialogue, leadership and diplomacy.

Emerging Leaders

Individuals developing their leadership careers may find the programme particularly useful for expanding their international exposure and connecting with other emerging leaders.

Changemakers and Innovators

The programme specifically describes itself as bringing together changemakers and innovators.

People working on innovative ideas, social initiatives or projects aimed at creating positive change may therefore find the international environment relevant.

Application Information and Required Details

The supplied application page indicates that applicants are required to provide several categories of personal and travel information.

The application form asks for:

  1. Full name as it appears on the passport.
  2. Gender.
  3. Date of birth.
  4. Nationality.
  5. Email address.
  6. Contact number.
  7. Country of residence.
  8. Departure city.
  9. Passport number.
  10. Whether a visa is required.
  11. Shirt size.
  12. Profile photograph.
  13. Passport or identification card.

The page specifies that profile photographs and passport/ID documents must be uploaded in JPG, JPEG, PNG, or PDF format, with a maximum file size of 1 MB for each upload field.

Applicants should therefore have the relevant personal and identification information available when completing the application.

Passport and Visa Information

The application form specifically asks applicants for their passport number and whether they need a visa.

This indicates that international travel documentation is an important part of the participation process.

Under the Direct Access Participation category, the organisers state that an invitation letter, sponsorship letter, embassy recommendation and visa-support documents will be provided.

However, participants should distinguish between visa support and a guaranteed visa approval. The supplied page states that visa-support documents will be provided, but it does not state that a Greek or Schengen visa is automatically guaranteed.

Applicants should therefore check the visa requirements applicable to their nationality and allow sufficient time for any necessary visa process.

Invitation and Sponsorship Letters

A major feature highlighted by the Direct Access Participation page is the provision of an invitation letter and sponsorship letter.

These documents are presented as part of the participation arrangement and are intended to support the participant’s international attendance.

The programme also states that an embassy recommendation and visa-support documents will be provided.

Applicants should carefully review the official participation terms to understand exactly what costs are covered by any sponsorship arrangement and which costs remain the participant’s responsibility. The supplied page does not provide a detailed breakdown of sponsorship coverage.

What Documents Should Applicants Prepare?

Based on the information requested on the application form, prospective participants should be prepared to provide:

  • Accurate passport details.
  • Personal identification information.
  • A profile photograph.
  • A copy of a passport or ID card.
  • Contact information.
  • Nationality information.
  • Country of residence.
  • Departure city.
  • Visa requirement information.

Applicants should ensure that their information is accurate and consistent with their official travel documents, particularly their full name and passport information.

Youth Envoys Greece 2027 Event Dates

The programme is scheduled for:

21–24 January 2027

The page describes this as a four-day session in Athens, Greece.

Participants planning to attend should take the full four-day schedule into account when arranging travel and accommodation.

Application Deadline

No application deadline is stated on the supplied page.

This is an important distinction for prospective applicants. Although the event dates are clearly provided as 21–24 January 2027, the supplied application page does not give a closing date for applications.

Applicants should therefore verify whether applications remain open and whether a separate deadline applies before making travel arrangements or submitting personal documentation.

How to Apply for Youth Envoy Greece 2027

The supplied page presents a direct application form for the Direct Access Participation category.

Interested participants can access the application through the programme page:

The application requires applicants to enter personal information and provide identification documents as part of the process.

Applicants should carefully review the form before submitting their information and ensure that all details correspond accurately with their passport or other official identification.

APPLY HERE

Important Things to Consider Before Applying

Although the programme advertises broad eligibility, applicants should carefully evaluate the participation arrangements before committing to international travel.

Consider the following:

1. Confirm the Current Application Status

Because no closing date is stated on the supplied page, applicants should confirm that applications are still being accepted.

2. Review Sponsorship Details

The page states that a sponsorship letter will be provided, but it does not give a detailed breakdown of what expenses are financially covered.

Applicants should clarify the scope of the sponsorship before assuming that flights, accommodation, meals, insurance or other expenses are fully covered.

3. Check Visa Requirements

The application asks whether a visa is required and states that visa-support documents will be provided.

Participants should independently check the applicable Greek/Schengen visa requirements for their nationality and plan accordingly.

4. Prepare Valid Identification

The application requests a passport or ID card upload and passport number.

Applicants should therefore ensure that their travel document information is accurate and that any required identification document is available in an accepted file format.

5. Plan for the Full Four-Day Programme

The event takes place from 21–24 January 2027.

Participants should plan their travel schedule around the entire programme rather than assuming that participation involves only a single day.

Frequently Asked Questions About Youth Envoys Greece 2027

What is Youth Envoys Greece 2027?

Youth Envoys Greece 2027 is a four-day international leadership and diplomacy programme scheduled to take place in Athens, Greece, from 21–24 January 2027.

Where will the programme take place?

The event will take place in Athens, Greece.

When will Youth Envoys Greece 2027 take place?

The programme is scheduled for 21–24 January 2027.

Is the programme open to international applicants?

Yes. The supplied page explicitly states that it is open to all nationalities.

Is there an age limit?

The page states that all ages are eligible.

Who can participate?

The programme mentions students, professionals, youth advocates, policymakers and emerging leaders, while also describing the intended community as including changemakers and innovators.

What is Direct Access Participation?

It is the participation category through which applicants can apply for a confirmed seat at the programme. The page states that an invitation letter, sponsorship letter, embassy recommendation and visa-support documents will be provided under this category.

Is a visa guaranteed?

The supplied page does not state that a visa is guaranteed. It states that visa-support documents will be provided. Applicants should separately confirm the visa requirements and approval process applicable to their nationality.

Is there an application deadline?

The supplied page does not state an application deadline. The event itself is scheduled for 21–24 January 2027.

What documents are requested during application?

The application form requests a profile photograph and a passport or ID card, in addition to personal, nationality, residence and travel information. The upload instructions allow JPG, JPEG, PNG, and PDF files up to 1 MB.

Do applicants need a particular academic qualification?

The supplied page does not state a specific academic qualification requirement.

Is there a specific race or ethnicity requirement?

No race or ethnicity requirement is stated on the supplied page. The programme instead states that it is open to all nationalities.

Visit HERE for more information about the Youth Envoys Greece 2027.

Conclusion

Youth Envoys Greece 2027 is an international leadership and diplomacy experience scheduled to bring participants to Athens, Greece, from 21–24 January 2027.

The Direct Access Participation category is particularly notable because the organisers state that participants will receive a confirmed seat together with an invitation letter, sponsorship letter, embassy recommendation and visa-support documents.

The opportunity has broad eligibility, with the programme stating that all nationalities and all ages are eligible. It is therefore not restricted to a particular country, continent, race or age group. Students, professionals, youth advocates, policymakers, changemakers, innovators and emerging leaders are among the participant profiles identified by the organisers.

For individuals interested in international leadership, diplomacy, networking and global engagement, the four-day Athens programme could provide an opportunity to connect with participants from different parts of the world and become part of an international community of changemakers.

However, prospective applicants should carefully examine the participation and sponsorship terms before committing financially. In particular, the supplied page does not provide a detailed breakdown of sponsorship coverage, nor does it state an application deadline. Applicants should verify these details directly with the organisers and confirm their individual visa requirements before making travel arrangements.

item.content:encoded:
The GIFTS – Global Institute Fellowship for Transforming Systems is a new global fellowship designed for influential education system leaders who are working to reshape education systems and create better futures for children and young people.

The fellowship brings together a carefully selected group of education system leaders from different countries for a year-long, cohort-based leadership and learning experience. Participants will have opportunities to engage with leading voices in education, collaborate with peers from around the world, receive mentoring and coaching, explore complex system-change challenges and participate in an in-person education-system immersion.

The programme is designed around the idea that education systems must evolve in response to major economic, technological and climatic changes while ensuring that every child has the opportunity to learn, thrive and develop the purpose, agency and abilities needed to shape a better future.

For education leaders working at a national or regional system level, the GIFTS Fellowship offers an opportunity to strengthen their leadership capabilities, expand their international networks, and develop locally rooted but globally informed approaches to education-system transformation.

What Is the GIFTS Global Institute Fellowship?

GIFTS stands for the Global Institute Fellowship for Transforming Systems.

It is a new fellowship created to address a gap experienced by education-system leaders who are working to transform complex education systems but may have limited opportunities to connect with other leaders facing similar challenges.

Education-system transformation can involve working across ministries, government institutions, schools, teachers, communities, civil society organisations and other stakeholders. Leaders responsible for this work must often navigate competing interests, political realities, changing technologies, economic pressures and evolving expectations about what education systems should deliver.

The GIFTS Fellowship is intended to create a global community in which such leaders can learn from one another, exchange experiences and develop the capabilities required to lead system-wide transformation.

The fellowship will bring together 20 influential education system insiders from diverse countries for a year-long experience combining virtual learning, peer engagement, mentoring, coaching and an in-person immersion.

Why Was the GIFTS Fellowship Created?

Education systems around the world are operating in an increasingly fast-changing environment.

Economic developments, technological advances and climate-related changes are creating new challenges and opportunities for education. At the same time, education systems are expected to ensure that children and young people develop not only academic capabilities but also the purpose and agency required to navigate an uncertain future.

The fellowship recognises that education-system leaders play a critical role in responding to these changes.

These leaders are expected to:

  • Chart new paths for their education systems.
  • Adapt institutions and strategies to changing realities.
  • Improve the performance of complex systems.
  • Mobilise people at different levels of the education system.
  • Inspire students, teachers and school leaders.
  • Work with government and other partners.
  • Address difficult system-level challenges.
  • Develop strategies capable of producing sustainable change.

Despite the importance and complexity of this work, education-system leaders may have relatively few opportunities to connect with peers, reflect on their experiences and share practical lessons about what it takes to transform education systems.

The GIFTS Fellowship has been launched to help address this gap by creating a structured global learning environment for education-system leaders.

What Will GIFTS Fellows Explore?

The fellowship will encourage participants to investigate fundamental questions about education-system transformation.

Among the questions highlighted by the programme are

  1. What outcomes should education systems achieve for all students today?
  2. How can the practices, structures and culture of an education system be aligned around its core purpose?
  3. What are the most effective strategies for improving the quality of learning in classrooms?
  4. What does improving classroom learning require from education-system leaders themselves?

These questions place system leadership at the centre of the fellowship.

Rather than looking only at individual schools or isolated education interventions, the programme focuses on the broader structures, practices, cultures and leadership approaches that determine how education systems operate.

Who Is the GIFTS Fellowship Designed For?

The GIFTS Fellowship is intended for influential and innovative education system leaders.

The programme specifically identifies leaders working within:

  • Ministries.
  • Political offices.
  • Civil society roles involving long-term partnerships with government.

This means the fellowship is targeted primarily at people who have the ability to influence education systems at a significant level.

It is not presented as a general scholarship or fellowship for students, recent graduates or people simply interested in education. Instead, the target participants are individuals already positioned within education systems or closely connected to government and capable of contributing to system-level transformation.

The programme seeks leaders who can demonstrate both a track record of commitment and the potential to influence education beyond their immediate organisation or role.

Qualities Expected of GIFTS Fellows

According to the fellowship information, successful fellows will demonstrate several important characteristics.

1. Commitment to Improving Systems Around Children

Fellows should have a lifelong commitment to improving the systems that shape children’s lives and educational experiences.

This means the programme is interested in leaders whose work goes beyond individual short-term interventions and is connected to improving the broader systems surrounding children.

2. Commitment to Holistic Student Development

Applicants should align with the purpose of developing all students holistically, regardless of their background or economic circumstances.

This reflects the fellowship’s emphasis on creating education systems that provide opportunities for every student rather than benefiting only particular groups.

3. Collective Leadership

Education-system transformation rarely happens through the work of one individual.

The fellowship therefore seeks leaders with the capacity to develop collective leadership and work effectively with others.

This can involve bringing together different stakeholders, building shared ownership and navigating the relationships necessary to move system-level initiatives forward.

4. Ability to Navigate Complex Politics

Transforming education systems can involve complex political and institutional environments.

The fellowship therefore looks for individuals capable of navigating political complexity while maintaining focus on system-level objectives.

5. Ability to Influence System-Level Change

Applicants should have the ability to influence significant change at a national or regional scale.

This is an important distinction because the fellowship is designed for system leaders whose influence extends beyond a single classroom, school or small community initiative.

6. Potential for Global Education Leadership

The programme also seeks individuals who have the potential to become influential leaders within the wider global education ecosystem.

This suggests that the fellowship is designed not only to strengthen participants’ current leadership but also to contribute to the development of a broader international community of education-system leaders.

What Does the GIFTS Fellowship Offer?

The fellowship provides a comprehensive learning and leadership experience lasting approximately one year.

The programme will combine several components, allowing fellows to learn through formal sessions, peer interaction, coaching, mentoring and practical exploration.

The major components include

  • A curated international cohort.
  • System Change Labs.
  • Virtual masterclasses.
  • Roundtables with senior education leaders.
  • Peer-learning groups.
  • Leadership sessions.
  • Mentoring.
  • Coaching.
  • A four-day in-person immersion.
  • The Better Future Forum.
  • Continued participation in a global community of system leaders.

Cohort-Based Learning Experience

The GIFTS Fellowship will bring together 20 education system leaders from diverse countries.

The cohort model is designed to create an environment in which participants can build trusting and enduring relationships with peers.

This peer network is particularly important because education-system leaders often face similar challenges even when they work in very different national contexts.

Through shared learning and reflection, fellows can exchange experiences and gain perspectives from leaders operating in other education systems.

The programme aims to create relationships that extend beyond the formal fellowship period and contribute to a lasting global community.

System Change Lab

The System Change Lab is a practical component of the fellowship.

Participants will explore and address a problem of practice during the fellowship. Rather than simply discussing system transformation at a theoretical level, fellows will have an opportunity to work on an issue connected to their own professional context.

The lab will use:

  • Action.
  • Reflection.
  • Peer feedback.
  • Exploration of practical challenges.
  • Generation of new insights.

This approach is intended to help fellows connect leadership learning with real system-level challenges.

Four-Day Education System Immersion

Another major component is the Immersion Event.

Fellows will participate in a four-day in-person immersive learning experience within an education system undergoing transformation.

The immersion will give participants opportunities to engage with:

  • Ministers.
  • Schools.
  • Practitioners.
  • Fellow participants.
  • Other education-system stakeholders.

The programme identifies the four-day immersion as required.

This practical exposure can enable fellows to observe system transformation in action and examine how leadership, policy, institutions and educational practice interact.

Masterclasses and Roundtables

Fellows will also participate in curated masterclasses and roundtable sessions involving senior global education leaders.

These are described as closed-door sessions where participants can engage in honest conversations about the realities of system transformation.

Topics can include:

  • Difficult trade-offs.
  • Failures.
  • Breakthroughs.
  • Leadership decisions.
  • System-level challenges.
  • Strategies for transformation.

The focus on honest dialogue is intended to create a learning environment where leaders can discuss not only successful initiatives but also the difficulties and failures that accompany complex system change.

Shared Inquiry and Peer Learning

The fellowship places significant emphasis on learning with and from peers.

Participants will form a curated cohort of education-system leaders and develop trusting relationships that support deeper learning.

Peer interaction can help fellows compare experiences across different contexts, question assumptions and explore alternative approaches to leadership and system transformation.

Triad Model Coaching

GIFTS will use a three-part coaching and support model.

The model brings together:

Policy Mentors

Policy mentors provide subject expertise and help participants think through policy-related questions and challenges.

Leadership Coaches

Leadership coaches support fellows as they navigate execution, uncertainty and difficult trade-offs associated with leadership.

Peer Coaches

Peer coaches contribute shared learning, accountability and feedback.

Together, these three forms of support are intended to provide a more comprehensive development experience, combining technical or policy expertise with leadership guidance and peer support.

The Better Future Forum

Fellows will also have an opportunity to participate in the Global Institute’s annual Better Future Forum.

The forum is an in-person event that provides an opportunity to connect with leaders from the global education ecosystem.

Participation in the Better Future Forum is listed as optional, unlike the four-day January immersion, which is specifically identified as required.

Building a Lifelong Global Community

The fellowship is designed to extend beyond the formal learning sessions.

Participants will have opportunities to exchange practices across geographical boundaries and may have the option of visiting other fellows.

The programme aims to build a lifelong global community of education-system leaders who can continue learning from one another and sharing practices after the formal fellowship concludes.

This international network is potentially one of the most valuable aspects of the programme for leaders working on complex education-system challenges.

GIFTS Fellowship 2026–2027 Timeline

The fellowship follows a year-long schedule beginning in 2026 and continuing through September 2027.

Application Stage

  • June 2026: Applications open.
  • 11 September 2026: Applications close.
  • October 2026: Selection announced.

Fellowship Journey

The fellowship programme then continues through a combination of virtual and in-person activities:

October 2026

  • Virtual launch event.

November–December 2026

  • Virtual lab.
  • Masterclasses.
  • Peer sessions.
  • Leadership sessions.

January 2027

  • Four-day in-person immersion event.
  • Attendance is required.

February–April 2027

  • Virtual lab.
  • Masterclasses.
  • Peer sessions.
  • Leadership sessions.

May 2027

  • Better Future Forum.
  • Three-day in-person event.
  • Participation is optional.

June–August 2027

  • Virtual lab.
  • Masterclasses.
  • Peer sessions.
  • Leadership sessions.

September 2027

  • Virtual graduation.

How to Apply for the GIFTS Fellowship

Individuals interested in the GIFTS Fellowship can submit an application through the fellowship’s application portal.

The programme asks applicants to refer to the application guidance contained in the fellowship blueprint document when preparing their applications.

Application deadline: 11 September 2026.

Prospective applicants should review the application guidance carefully and ensure that their experience and leadership profile clearly demonstrate the qualities sought by the fellowship.

APPLY HERE

Nominations Are Also Welcome

The GIFTS Fellowship does not rely solely on self-nomination.

The organisers also welcome nominations of exceptional system leaders who are working at the forefront of education-system transformation and shaping a better future for children and young people.

However, a nomination is not an application and does not guarantee selection.

If a nominee appears to meet the fellowship’s eligibility criteria, they may subsequently be invited to submit a full application.

Submit a GIFTS Fellowship Nomination

This nomination route creates an opportunity for organisations, colleagues and other stakeholders to identify education leaders whose work deserves consideration.

Global Eligibility and Geographic Reach

The GIFTS Fellowship is explicitly described as a global fellowship.

The programme aims to bring together education-system leaders from countries around the world and states that the cohort will include leaders from diverse countries.

The supplied information does not provide a specific list of eligible countries or continents. It also does not identify any race or ethnicity restrictions.

Therefore, the opportunity should be understood as internationally oriented, while applicants should consult the official application guidance to determine whether any additional eligibility conditions apply.

What Kind of Leader Is Best Suited to GIFTS?

The GIFTS Fellowship is particularly suited to an education professional who is already working on system-level change rather than someone who is simply beginning a career in education.

A potentially strong candidate would be someone whose work involves influencing education policy, institutions, government systems, regional or national education strategies, or long-term government partnerships.

The fellowship may be particularly relevant to leaders who are:

  • Working within education ministries.
  • Working within political offices connected to education.
  • Leading civil society initiatives in long-term partnership with government.
  • Influencing education policy or system reform.
  • Working on national or regional education transformation.
  • Building collective leadership across complex education systems.
  • Developing innovative approaches to improving outcomes for children.
  • Seeking to strengthen their international education leadership network.

The programme’s stated eligibility profile places considerable emphasis on influence, innovation, system-level change and leadership potential.

Programme Commitments and Participation

The fellowship involves a mixture of virtual and in-person activities spread across approximately one year.

Participants should therefore be prepared to engage consistently with the fellowship journey.

The programme includes recurring virtual labs, masterclasses, peer and leadership sessions, as well as the required four-day in-person immersion in January 2027. The Better Future Forum in May 2027 is identified as optional.

The supplied source also points applicants toward a separate programme information document containing additional details concerning the curriculum, faculty and fellowship commitments.

View the GIFTS Programme Information, Curriculum and Fellowship Commitments

Why the GIFTS Fellowship Could Be Valuable for Education Leaders

Education-system leaders often work in environments where change is difficult because systems involve many interconnected institutions and stakeholders.

A change in one part of an education system can have consequences elsewhere. Leaders may therefore need to balance policy objectives, institutional realities, stakeholder interests, political considerations and the needs of students.

The GIFTS Fellowship is structured around precisely these kinds of challenges.

Its combination of peer learning, system-change work, mentoring, leadership coaching and exposure to other education systems can provide participants with multiple perspectives on how large-scale transformation can be approached.

The international cohort also creates an opportunity to compare approaches across countries and learn how different leaders respond to similar challenges in different contexts.

Important Information for Prospective Applicants

Before applying or accepting a nomination, prospective fellows should carefully review the official programme guidance.

In particular, applicants should pay attention to:

  1. The eligibility profile: The programme is seeking influential and innovative education-system leaders rather than applicants at any career stage.
  2. Leadership experience: Applicants should be able to demonstrate their capacity to influence system-level change at national or regional scale.
  3. Government connection: The programme specifically identifies people working within ministries, political offices or civil society roles involving long-term government partnerships.
  4. International orientation: The fellowship brings together leaders from diverse countries and is designed to develop a global community.
  5. Time commitment: The programme runs for approximately one year and involves virtual and in-person activities.
  6. Required immersion: The four-day January 2027 in-person immersion is listed as required.
  7. Optional forum: The three-day Better Future Forum in May 2027 is listed as optional.
  8. Application deadline: Applications close on 11 September 2026.
  9. Nominations: A nomination does not constitute an application and does not guarantee selection.

Visit HERE for more information about the GIFTS Global Institute Fellowship 2026–2027.

Frequently Asked Questions About the GIFTS Global Institute Fellowship

What does GIFTS stand for?

GIFTS stands for Global Institute Fellowship for Transforming Systems.

Who is the fellowship for?

It is designed for influential and innovative education-system leaders working within ministries, political offices or civil society roles that involve long-term partnerships with government.

How many fellows will be selected?

The fellowship will bring together 20 influential education system insiders from diverse countries.

How long does the fellowship last?

The GIFTS Fellowship is structured as a year-long cohort-based experience, beginning with the virtual launch in October 2026 and concluding with virtual graduation in September 2027.

When is the application deadline?

Applications close on 11 September 2026.

Is the fellowship open internationally?

The programme is explicitly described as a global fellowship and intends to bring together leaders from diverse countries around the world. The supplied source does not provide a specific list of eligible countries.

Are nominations accepted?

Yes. The organisers welcome nominations of exceptional education-system leaders. However, a nomination does not guarantee selection and is not itself an application. A nominee who appears to meet the eligibility criteria may be invited to submit a full application.

Is the in-person immersion mandatory?

Yes. The January 2027 immersion is described as a four-day in-person event and required.

Is the Better Future Forum mandatory?

The source identifies the May 2027 Better Future Forum as a three-day in-person event that is optional.

What kind of coaching is offered?

The fellowship uses a triad model combining policy mentors for subject expertise, leadership coaches for navigating execution and uncertainty, and peer coaches for shared learning, accountability and feedback.

What is the System Change Lab?

It is a fellowship component through which participants explore and address a problem of practice, generating insights through action, reflection and peer feedback.

Conclusion

The GIFTS Global Institute Fellowship for Transforming Systems is a global leadership opportunity for education-system leaders who are working to create meaningful and sustainable change at a national or regional scale.

The fellowship goes beyond conventional professional development by bringing together a select cohort of 20 influential education leaders for a year-long experience combining peer learning, system-change work, global masterclasses, mentoring, leadership coaching and practical immersion.

Its focus is particularly relevant to leaders who work within ministries, political offices or civil society organisations engaged in long-term partnerships with government. The programme seeks people who demonstrate a sustained commitment to improving systems around children, can develop collective leadership, can navigate complex political environments and have the ability to influence significant education-system change.

For successful fellows, the experience is designed to strengthen their leadership capabilities, broaden their global perspective, develop new insights into system transformation and connect them with a lifelong international community of education-system leaders.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the 2027 Democratic Alliance (DA) Young Leaders Programme (YLP), a one-year political leadership learning and development programme designed for young South Africans who are passionate about leadership, public service, politics and creating positive change in their communities.

The programme provides an opportunity for motivated young people to strengthen their political knowledge, critical-thinking abilities, communication skills and personal leadership capabilities while gaining practical experience through a dedicated leadership project.

For young South Africans considering a future in politics, government, public service or community leadership, the DA Young Leaders Programme offers structured leadership development designed to help participants understand their leadership potential, identify areas for personal growth, and develop the skills required to become effective changemakers.

About the DA Young Leaders Programme 2027

The DA Young Leaders Programme is described as a political leadership learning and development programme for South Africans aged between 18 and 35 who align themselves with the Democratic Alliance’s values of Freedom, Fairness, Opportunity and Diversity.

The programme is aimed at highly motivated individuals who are interested in pursuing a career in politics or the public service and who want to contribute to building what the DA describes as “One Nation with One Future.”

Rather than focusing only on theoretical leadership concepts, the programme combines political learning, personal development, communication development and practical leadership experience. Participants are expected to develop a stronger understanding of politics while also gaining greater insight into their own leadership style, strengths and development needs.

Over the course of one year, Young Leaders participate in activities intended to broaden their political knowledge and critical-thinking capabilities. They also develop communication skills and take part in dedicated sessions focused on leadership and personal development.

A central component of the programme is the requirement for each participant to conceptualise and undertake a leadership project. This gives participants an opportunity to apply what they learn in a practical setting while addressing an issue within their community.

Who Should Apply for the DA Young Leaders Programme?

The programme is designed for young people who are not only interested in leadership but are already demonstrating a commitment to making a positive difference in their communities.

According to the programme information, successful applicants are expected to demonstrate qualities such as

  • Integrity and a strong commitment to serving others.
  • Leadership potential and motivation to create meaningful change.
  • A desire to continue developing their personal and professional potential.
  • An interest in politics, public service or government as a potential career path.
  • A passion for contributing to a better future for South Africa.
  • The ability to align their personal values with the Democratic Alliance’s liberal values and principles.
  • An interest in strengthening their critical-thinking, communication, writing, public-speaking, and leadership skills.

The programme therefore goes beyond identifying young people who simply have an interest in politics. It seeks individuals who demonstrate leadership potential, community commitment and a willingness to take responsibility for creating meaningful change.

What Participants Can Gain from the Young Leaders Programme

The DA Young Leaders Programme provides a combination of political education, leadership development, personal development and practical experience.

1. Political Knowledge and Understanding

Participants have the opportunity to broaden their understanding of politics and develop greater political knowledge. This can help them better understand the issues affecting South Africa and the role that effective leadership can play in addressing national and community challenges.

The political learning component is particularly relevant for young people considering future careers in political leadership, government or public service.

2. Critical-Thinking Skills

Critical thinking is another important area of development within the programme.

Participants are challenged to think critically and develop the ability to engage with issues in a thoughtful and informed manner. These skills can be valuable for people interested in policy, public leadership, government and community development.

3. Communication Development

Communication is a major component of effective leadership, and the programme provides participants with opportunities to strengthen their communication abilities.

Participants are expected to develop their:

  • Writing skills
  • Public-speaking abilities
  • General communication skills
  • Ability to express ideas effectively
  • Capacity to engage with political and community issues

These skills can be particularly valuable for aspiring public representatives and future leaders.

4. Personal Leadership Development

The programme also places considerable emphasis on personal development.

Participants are given opportunities to understand themselves better, including their individual leadership styles and areas where they need further development. Dedicated leadership and personal-development sessions are intended to support this process.

This emphasis means that the programme is not solely focused on external leadership responsibilities. It also encourages participants to develop self-awareness and understand how their individual characteristics can influence the way they lead.

5. Practical Leadership Experience

One of the distinguishing elements of the programme is the leadership project that every participant is required to undertake.

Through this project, participants are able to move beyond classroom or theoretical learning and apply their leadership skills to a real-world challenge.

The programme states that these projects provide experience in areas such as:

  • Planning
  • Collaboration
  • Community engagement
  • Leadership
  • Problem-solving
  • Public leadership

This practical experience can help participants build confidence and develop a stronger understanding of what effective leadership looks like in real communities.

Leadership in Action: The Programme’s Community Projects

The leadership project component is intended to create meaningful impact within participants’ communities.

According to the programme information, previous projects have addressed a range of social and community challenges. Examples provided by the programme include initiatives focused on gender-based violence awareness, school support, youth employment, housing and education.

Examples include:

Anti-Gender-Based Violence Awareness

Some Young Leaders have developed campaigns focused on raising awareness about gender-based violence. These initiatives have included empowering young women and organising public gatherings against gender-based violence.

Such projects demonstrate how leadership development can be connected to advocacy and community mobilisation.

School Support Initiatives

Other projects have focused on supporting disadvantaged schoolchildren.

The examples include initiatives that provided children with essential items such as proper shoes, with the broader aim of supporting their confidence and sense of pride.

Female Youth Employment Projects

Some participants have worked on projects designed to address youth employment challenges among disadvantaged girls.

These initiatives have sought to help bridge the gap between secondary education and full-time employment, demonstrating how Young Leaders can use community projects to address barriers facing young people.

Housing and Education Projects

Other leadership projects have addressed housing and community resilience.

The programme highlights projects involving the construction of houses in vulnerable areas of the Western Cape, alongside efforts to educate local communities about the use of sandbag systems for flood protection.

These examples illustrate the practical dimension of the Young Leaders Programme: participants are expected to use their leadership skills to engage with genuine challenges and develop initiatives that can produce tangible community benefits.

The DA Young Leaders Programme’s Long-Term Impact

The Young Leaders Programme has already developed a substantial alumni network.

According to the programme’s information, more than 330 graduates have completed the programme since its launch. These alumni are described as making an impact across South Africa in public office, within the Democratic Alliance and through community initiatives.

The programme reports the following impact figures:

  • 330+ graduates have completed the Young Leaders Programme.
  • 84 alumni are currently serving in public office, including as Members of Parliament, Members of Provincial Legislatures, councillors and other elected representatives.
  • 7 members of the Democratic Alliance’s leadership are alumni of the Young Leaders Programme.
  • Alumni continue to contribute through community initiatives, public service and policy development across South Africa.

These figures demonstrate the programme’s stated role in developing a pipeline of young people who can go on to participate in political leadership, public service and community development.

The Programme’s Vision for South Africa

The Young Leaders Programme is connected to the DA’s broader vision for South Africa.

The programme’s stated vision is for a South Africa in which individuals have the opportunity to live lives that they value. It describes a country characterised by a dynamic and innovative society, an inclusive and growing economy, and a capable government that protects the Constitution and promotes equal opportunity.

The vision emphasises equal opportunity regardless of where people are born, how they look or other arbitrary characteristics.

The programme argues that achieving such a vision requires excellent leaders who are prepared to step forward and lead.

Consequently, the Young Leaders Programme is positioned as part of the effort to prepare young South Africans for future leadership responsibilities.

Eligibility for the DA Young Leaders Programme 2027

The source identifies the programme as being open to South Africans between the ages of 18 and 35 who align with the DA’s stated values of Freedom, Fairness, Opportunity and Diversity.

Potential applicants should therefore carefully consider whether they meet the programme’s stated target profile before submitting an application.

The programme is particularly relevant to individuals who:

  1. Are South African.
  2. Are aged between 18 and 35.
  3. Are interested in politics, government or public service.
  4. Demonstrate leadership potential.
  5. Are already making a positive impact in their communities.
  6. Demonstrate integrity and a commitment to serving others.
  7. Want to strengthen their political knowledge and critical-thinking skills.
  8. Want to improve their writing, public-speaking, and communication abilities.
  9. Are willing to undertake a leadership project.
  10. Can align their personal values with the DA’s stated liberal values and principles.

The source also lists a series of frequently asked questions concerning matters such as time commitment, age requirements, participation while working or studying full-time, retreats, transportation, leadership projects, costs, selection numbers, tertiary qualifications, previous applications and prior participation in other DA leadership programmes. However, the supplied source does not provide the answers to those questions, so applicants should not assume requirements or conditions that are not expressly stated.

Is a Tertiary Qualification Required?

The programme’s webpage includes a frequently asked question specifically asking whether applicants need a tertiary qualification to apply.

However, the supplied material lists the question without providing an answer. Therefore, the source does not establish that a university or college qualification is either required or not required.

Applicants who are concerned about this requirement should verify the current application instructions before submitting their applications rather than relying on assumptions.

Previous Applicants and DA Programme Participants

The programme information also includes frequently asked questions about whether people who previously applied unsuccessfully can apply again and whether individuals who have already participated in another DA leadership programme can apply.

Again, the supplied source lists these questions but does not provide their answers. Applicants in either situation should therefore consult the official programme information or contact the YLP Office for clarification.

What Makes the Programme Relevant to Aspiring Public Leaders?

Leadership in politics and public service requires more than an interest in public affairs. Effective leaders need to communicate ideas, understand complex issues, work with others, engage communities and develop the confidence to make decisions.

The Young Leaders Programme brings these areas together through political learning, critical thinking, communication development, personal leadership sessions and practical community projects.

For young people considering a future in political or public leadership, the programme can therefore provide a structured environment in which to explore leadership ambitions while developing practical skills.

Its emphasis on leadership projects is particularly significant because participants are expected to translate their learning into action. Rather than limiting leadership development to discussions and training sessions, the programme provides an opportunity to work on a real community challenge.

Why Community Leadership Experience Matters

The programme’s emphasis on community projects reflects the importance of practical experience in leadership development.

Working on a community initiative can require a participant to identify a problem, understand the people affected, develop an approach, work with others and implement activities. Such an experience can strengthen a range of leadership capabilities.

The examples provided by the programme show that leadership projects can cover diverse areas, including social justice, education, employment, housing, gender-based violence awareness and community resilience.

This provides participants with an opportunity to connect leadership development with issues that affect communities directly.

Application Deadline for the DA Young Leaders Programme 2027

The application deadline is: 25th September 2026

Applications for the 2027 Young Leaders Programme opened on 1st September 2026, and applicants are encouraged to submit their applications before the stated closing date.

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day to apply. Preparing application information in advance can give prospective candidates sufficient time to review their submission and ensure that all required information has been provided.

How to Apply for the DA Young Leaders Programme 2027

Interested applicants can submit their applications through the programme’s official application portal.

Application deadline: 25 September 2026

The official programme page also directs prospective applicants to the application portal and provides additional information about the Young Leaders Programme.

APPLY HERE

Important Considerations Before Applying

Prospective applicants should carefully assess their motivation and leadership goals before applying.

A strong candidate for this programme should be able to demonstrate more than an interest in obtaining leadership training. The programme is aimed at young people who want to contribute to their communities and potentially pursue careers in politics or public service.

Before applying, applicants should consider:

  • Why they are interested in political or public leadership.
  • How they have demonstrated leadership in their community.
  • What social or community issues they are passionate about addressing.
  • How their personal values align with the programme’s stated values.
  • How they would use improved communication and leadership skills.
  • What kind of community leadership project they could potentially undertake.
  • How participation in the programme fits into their longer-term career aspirations.

The programme’s emphasis on personal development also means that applicants should be prepared to reflect on their own strengths, leadership style and areas for improvement.

Frequently Asked Questions About the DA Young Leaders Programme 2027

What is the DA Young Leaders Programme?

The DA Young Leaders Programme is a one-year political leadership learning and development programme for South Africans aged 18 to 35 who align with the Democratic Alliance’s stated values and are interested in politics or public service.

Who can apply?

The programme is intended for South Africans between the ages of 18 and 35 who demonstrate leadership potential, community commitment and an interest in politics, government or public service. Applicants should also align with the programme’s stated values.

What skills can participants develop?

Participants can develop political knowledge, critical thinking, communication, writing, public speaking, and leadership skills. The programme also provides opportunities for personal development and greater self-awareness.

Do participants undertake a practical project?

Yes. Every participant is required to conceptualise and undertake a leadership project designed to create meaningful impact within their community.

What types of projects have previous Young Leaders undertaken?

Examples provided by the programme include gender-based violence awareness campaigns, school support programmes, female youth employment initiatives, housing projects and education initiatives focused on community flood protection.

How many people have graduated from the programme?

The programme reports that more than 330 people have graduated from the Young Leaders Programme since its launch. It also reports that 84 alumni are currently serving in public office and that seven members of DA leadership are programme alumni.

When does the 2027 application close?

Applications close on 25 September 2026.

Is the programme only for people already active in the DA?

The programme’s FAQ section specifically asks whether applicants need to be actively involved in the DA, but the supplied source does not provide the answer. Applicants should therefore verify the current requirement directly with the programme office.

Is a tertiary qualification required?

The source asks whether applicants need a tertiary qualification but does not provide an answer. This requirement should therefore be confirmed through the official programme information before applying.

Visit HERE for more information about the DA Young Leaders Programme 2027.

Conclusion

The DA Young Leaders Programme 2027 presents an opportunity for young South Africans aged 18 to 35 who are interested in political leadership, public service, government and community development to undertake a structured year of leadership learning and personal development.

The programme combines political knowledge, critical thinking, communication development and personal leadership training with practical experience through a required community leadership project. Its stated objective is to help participants better understand their own leadership capabilities while equipping them with the knowledge, confidence and skills needed to increase their impact in their communities and potentially pursue leadership roles on a broader stage.

The programme’s reported alumni impact, including more than 330 graduates and 84 alumni currently serving in public office, further highlights its stated contribution to developing young leaders who have gone on to participate in public and political leadership.

For eligible young South Africans who are passionate about making a difference, interested in politics or public service, and committed to developing their leadership potential, the 2027 intake may be worth considering.

For more global Fellowship opportunities, visit OFY HERE.

The Green Climate Fund (GCF) is the world’s largest dedicated climate fund, empowering developing countries to build a low-emission, climate-resilient future. As climate solutions scale globally, GCF continues to expand its workforce—creating exceptional opportunities for students, young professionals, and experienced experts.

Headquartered in Songdo, Incheon, Republic of Korea, GCF offers a dynamic, international work environment in one of Asia’s most modern and vibrant smart cities.

Why Join the Green Climate Fund?

GCF looks for individuals who:

  • Think strategically and execute with purpose

  • Communicate clearly and collaborate effectively

  • Bring diverse academic, cultural, and professional perspectives

  • Thrive in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment

The GCF Careers Portal outlines its culture, benefits, and commitment to diversity, inclusion, transparency, and respect.

The GCF Internship Programme (Paid)

The GCF Internship Programme is designed for highly motivated Master’s and PhD students, as well as recent graduates, from all backgrounds. The Fund strongly encourages applications from nationals of developing countries and individuals with diverse academic and cultural experiences.

Internship Benefits

  • USD 1,600 monthly stipend

  • Free global health insurance

  • Roundtrip airfare for international interns

  • Full-time, on-site work at GCF headquarters

  • 6-month contract, extendable to 12 months based on performance

  • Immersive experience in a multicultural, high-impact climate institution

Internship Eligibility Criteria

To qualify, applicants must:

  • Be enrolled in a Master’s or PhD programme, or be a recent graduate

  • Have academic training relevant to GCF’s mission (climate, environment, finance, data, law, policy, engineering, IT, communications, etc.)

  • Demonstrate excellent English proficiency

  • Be available to work on-site in Songdo, South Korea

Internship Recruitment Timeline (Annual Cycle)

  • December – Early January: Internship applications open

  • February – May: Screening, assessments, and interviews

  • July: Cohort begins (individual start dates may vary)

Selection Process

  1. CV Screening

  2. Online video interview and/or written assessment

  3. Final 30-minute online panel interview

GCF Internship Opportunities 

Below are internship roles available:

Intern – IT Department – Click here for full details 

New Oracle Recruitment Platform

GCF now uses a streamlined, modern Oracle-based recruitment system, allowing applicants to:

  • Create/update profiles

  • Submit applications easily

  • Track application progress in real-time

How to Apply

If you’re inspired by GCF’s mission and believe your profile aligns with the Fund’s work:

👉 Visit the GCF Careers Portal
👉 Explore current internship 
👉 Create or update your profile in the Oracle recruitment system
👉 Submit all required documents before the deadline

Need Help?

If you have any questions about the application or recruitment process, please contact:
📩 recruitment@gcfund.org

Internship Summary

  • Category: Internships

  • Location: Songdo, Incheon, South Korea

  • Schedule: Full-time

  • Degree Level: Master’s (or enrolled / recent graduate)

  • Stipend / Minimum Salary: USD 1,600 per month

  • Contract Duration: 6 months, extendable to 12

  • Work Arrangement: Fully on-site at GCF Headquarters

Final Thoughts

The GCF Internship Programme is one of the most competitive and influential opportunities for emerging leaders in climate finance, sustainable development, environmental science, policy, data, and global governance. With world-class mentorship, generous benefits, and meaningful climate impact work, GCF offers a powerful platform to launch or elevate your career.

Don’t miss this chance to be part of a dynamic, multicultural environment, contributing to impactful climate initiatives. Join us in shaping a sustainable future through the GCF Internship Program!

item.content:encoded:
Are you a young graduate interested in international relations, diplomacy, European affairs, politics, communications, environment, economics or public policy? The European Union Delegation to the United States is offering funded traineeships for young graduates across several sections of its Washington, D.C. delegation.

The traineeships can last up to six months, with the tentative start date set for November 2026, subject to budget availability.

Application deadline: 14 September 2026.

EU Delegation USA Funded Traineeships 2026 – Quick Overview

Opportunity Details
Host organisation EU Delegation to the United States
Location United States of America
Duration Up to 6 months
Tentative start November 2026
Category Traineeship
Funding Monthly grant
Deadline 14 September 2026
Eligibility Young graduates with at least a Bachelor’s degree
Language Excellent English
Work schedule Full-time, Monday–Friday

Are you a young graduate interested in international relations? Are you curious to learn more about work of a diplomatic mission and how the EU Delegation represents EU interests and values in United States of America?

What is offered:

Traineeships of up to 6 months within the following sections of the EU Delegation to the United States, subject to availability of the budget. The tentative start date is November 2026.

Traineeship in the Administration Section (ADMIN):

The Administration section provides support services to the Delegation staff, building, and residences. It encompasses Human Resources, Accounting & Finance, Infrastructure, and Information Technology. It liaises with authorities in Europe and the United States on protocol and administrative matters related to EU officials. As a trainee in the Admin section, you will work on the following tasks:

Main tasks:

  • Support the logistical coordination and organization of meetings, events, workshops, and official visits, including escorting visitors to the Delegation.
  • Receive, organize, and maintain office stationery, supplies, and other materials.
  • Maintain accurate records of suppliers, orders, deliveries, and expenditures.
  • Provide general administrative and clerical support to the Section, including filing, correspondence, scheduling, and document management.
  • Attend internal and external meetings and prepare minutes, action points, and follow-up records.
  • Assist with maintaining organized records and ensuring that administrative activities are completed efficiently and on time.
  • Assist with market surveys

Traineeship in the Global Issues and Innovation section (GIN):

The Global Issues and Innovation section monitors and analyses U.S. political, economic, and regulatory developments in the areas of transportation, energy and environment, research and innovation, space, food safety (which includes plant and animal health and animal welfare), public health, and consumer protection. As a trainee in the Global Issues and Innovation section, you will work on the following tasks:

Main tasks:

  • Researching U.S. regulatory developments in the areas of transportation, climate, energy and environment, research and innovation, space, food safety, public health, and consumer protection.
  • Attending U.S. Congressional hearings and other public events related to section policy areas and writing summaries for the section.
  • Support the preparation of the Delegation’s outreach activities within the GIN section areas.
  • Preparing minutes of section meetings.

Traineeship in the Head of Delegation section (HOD):

The Head of Delegation Section (HOD) supports the work of both the Ambassador and Deputy Ambassador in promoting positive relations with the United States.

The HOD team coordinates with all Sections across the Delegation to establish priorities for the Ambassador’s agenda, ensure briefing for all scheduled meetings and engagements, coordinate a high number of social and diplomatic functions at the EU residence (dinners, lunches, receptions and events), and plan several State Outreach visits per year to build relationships at the State level with elected officials, business leaders and civil society. The HOD team also works with the wider Delegation to ensure the Ambassador’s participation in all high-level visits from Headquarters, and prepares the monthly coordination meetings of EU Ambassadors and Deputy Ambassadors as well as a monthly briefing call with EU Consuls General serving as EU Local Chairs around the US. The HOD intern will primarily be tasked to assist on State Outreach planning and events hosted by the Ambassador at the official EU Residence. As a trainee in the HOD section, you will work on the following tasks:

Main tasks:

  • State Outreach:
    • Conducting preliminary research to identify suitable meetings/events/partner in the destination State
    • Assisting with pre-trip planning calls with contacts in the destination State
    • Briefing assembly
    • Post-trip follow-up correspondence
  • Support to Social Secretary for Events at EU Residence
  • Ad Hoc special projects at request of Ambassador

Traineeship in the Political section (POL):

The Political Section follows all aspects of the transatlantic agenda and closely monitors the work of Congress and the U.S. Administration on foreign, security, and defence policy, counterterrorism and home affairs, and human rights, as well as U.S. domestic policy and U.S. elections. The section maintains regular contact with a broad range of Washington-based NGOs, think tanks, and civil society organizations. As a trainee in the Political section, you will work on the following tasks:

Main tasks:

  • Attending virtual U.S. Congressional hearings and writing summaries.
  • Attending think tank events and writing summaries of topics covered.
  • Researching and writing reports on foreign policy, security, and development cooperation issues for the section.
  • Contributing to briefings on issues related to the section’s priorities.
  • Assisting with the organization of outreach events and activities related to political, security and development issues.

Traineeship in the Press and Public Diplomacy section (PPD):

The Press and Public Diplomacy section aims to highlight the work of the EU to various audiences in the U.S. As a horizontal section, PPD is the key coordinator of all the Delegation’s public outreach activities. The section is also responsible for the Delegation’s media relations and communications strategy. In addition, the section manages people-to-people initiatives and is in charge of the EU’s cultural diplomacy in the U.S. As a trainee in the Press and Public Diplomacy section, you will work on the following tasks:

Main tasks:

  • Assisting with the organization of public diplomacy events.
  • Assisting with media monitoring and analysis and support for press events.
  • Supporting the section with social media communication and digital content creation (website and social media).
  • Monitoring events organized by think tanks and other organizations for reporting purposes.
  • Providing research assistance as needed in areas related to the section’s priorities.
  • Preparing minutes of meetings and assisting with drafting briefings.
  • Answering general information requests.

Qualifications or special requirements:

  • Must have at least a Bachelor’s Diploma and background in relevant disciplines (International Affairs, European Affairs, Political Science, Law, Communications, Environment, Health, Science, Economics and other related policy areas).
  • Excellent command of the English language.
  • Be available full time, Monday through Friday.

How to apply?

Candidates must apply to the e-mail address delegation-usa-internships@eeas.europa.eu and send the following documents:

  • A detailed standard Europass curriculum vitae (CV) https://europa.eu/europass/en (CVs in other format will not be considered)
  • a cover letter describing why you want to participate in a EU traineeship
  • and an application form

Please mention in the subject of your e-mail: Funded Traineeship – ADMIN, GIN, HOD, POL, or PPD (you may only apply to 1 traineeship per delegation, however based on your profile, the delegation could offer you a traineeship in another section).

Important information to read before applying

Before applying you are requested to examine the dedicated website as well as the general eligibility criteria for a paid traineeship (Article 8 of the Decision ADMIN(2017)28 – Paid traineeship).

Each selected trainee will receive a monthly grant to cover living expenses. All costs related to travels, visa, insurance, accommodation must be borne by the trainee.

Applications from non-eligible candidates will not be considered. After the evaluation of all applications, shortlisted candidates will be contacted and invited for an interview. Unsuccessful candidates will be notified by email. In case the selected candidates are not able to present the required documents, their application will be rejected.

The traineeships can only be offered in compliance with the local legislation as well as the legislation of the country of origin. 

Citizens from EU Member states:

  • must provide proof that they will be covered against the risk of a pandemic and the costs of repatriation;

  • must hold a relevant entrance visa and / or temporary residence permit where applicable, based on the traineeship agreement, the duration of the traineeship, and in compliance with the local legislation.
